correctness.rationale: The exact killed Brownian Green density, event probabilities, OU negative-return time change, n-th moment normal integral with integrable domination, compact positive-return exit bounds, and regenerative binomial recurrence prove k^(n-1/2)E(T^n)→c_n for every fixed r>0 and n≥1. The key p0=H_r cancellation is derived via optional stopping. The proof distinguishes finite numerical checks from infinite asymptotics and specifies all boundaries.

limitations: The theorem holds at each fixed r>0; no joint (r,k) limit or full distributional limit.
Earlier mean-return formulas and the OU hitting transform are known; only the all-moment completion-time asymptotics and consequences are assessed as new.

value.rationale: The experimentally natural finite-return protocol lacks a quantitative weak-return-stiffness precision law in the inspected mean-centered sources. The full integer-moment spectrum and reset-rate-independent leading amplitudes expose strong non-self-averaging of the physical completion clock; in particular variance grows faster than squared mean and the coefficient of variation diverges. This sharp observable boundary is not a routine evaluation of an arbitrary slice or a known first-moment table.
